⁣
More than 25 years after its release, this movie somehow feels more relevant than ever. I still remember watching it for the first time as a kid, expecting cool action and special effects. Instead, I got a movie that genuinely made me question reality. ⁣
⁣
Morpheus asks one simple question: what is real? That question is at the heart of everything. In 1999, this whole thing was merely science fiction. Today, AI is developing at incredible speed, while governments and technology companies are debating questions that sound surprisingly familiar: Who controls these systems? How do we keep them aligned with human interests? And what happens if technology develops faster than our ability to understand or regulate it?⁣
⁣
That doesn’t mean The Matrix literally predicted our future. Its genius is that it understood something timeless about humanity: we build powerful systems first and often worry about the consequences later.⁣
⁣

source_details.synopsis: The Matrix is a 1999 science fiction–action film written and directed by the Wachowskis. The first installment in the Matrix film series, it stars Keanu Reeves, Laurence Fishburne, Carrie-Anne Moss, Hugo Weaving, and Joe Pantoliano. The film follows a disillusioned computer hacker Neo (Reeves) who discovers that the life he knows is an elaborate deception created by intelligent machines. He is recruited by underground insurgents Morpheus (Fishburne) and Trinity (Moss), to join the rebellion against the machines.
